A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ThinkAct and contain complete, readable main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–B, and references. Their corresponding content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original robot-manipulation and embodied-reasoning evaluations, including benchmark scores, reward ablations, few-shot adaptation, and self-correction examples in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including the 84.4% overall LIBERO success rate in Table 1.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same dual-system architecture, action-aligned rewards, GRPO training, latent-plan conditioning, and inference procedure. Table A5's model-name correction does not change the method.

E1.justification: Training data coverage in Section 4.1 and Appendix A is unchanged. Evaluation retains SimplerEnv, LIBERO, EgoPlan-Bench2, RoboVQA, and OpenEQA, including the same few-shot and failure-recovery scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 2, and A5 and the few-shot comparisons. Table A5 changes the authors' own column label from ThinkVLA-3B to ThinkAct-3B; it does not introduce or replace a comparator.

E3.justification: The benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets, model sizes, preprocessing, and evaluation procedures match. Both versions retain the same 5-shot and 10-shot LIBERO experiments with 100 evaluation trials.

E4.justification: The reward ablations, reasoning-frequency analysis, smaller-model evaluation, few-shot analyses, self-correction examples, and inference-speed comparison are retained unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 specifies three random seeds for LIBERO in both versions. There are no changes to repeated-run disclosures or additions of confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results match. LIBERO overall success remains 84.4% in Table 1; Table A5 retains aggregate scores of 44.0, 55.3, and 48.9 despite its corrected model label.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, reward equations, GRPO objective, and imitation-learning loss in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about reinforced visual latent planning, few-shot adaptation, long-horizon planning, and self-correction.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the reward ablations, reasoning frequency, and inference-cost tradeoff are unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning inherited visual/spatial hallucinations and their effects on action execution.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain identical hyperparameters, hardware, data-construction instructions, and prompt content. The project-page link and supplementary-video reference are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 56 references and related-work discussions are retained. Positioning relative to end-to-end VLAs, supervised reasoning approaches, and reinforcement-based visual reasoning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Table A5 corrects ThinkVLA-3B to ThinkAct-3B, and the first-page date and arXiv version markings are updated. Otherwise, wording and document organization remain unchanged apart from minor line wrapping.

P2.justification: Table A5's corrected column heading accompanies slight table-spacing and downstream placement adjustments. Minor text reflow also occurs, including in Table A4. No figures or tables are added, removed, or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes a naming inconsistency in Table A5, whose column was already identified as the authors' model by '(Ours)' and Appendix B.4. This small editorial correction and the date/typesetting updates leave scientific evidence, clarity of the overall argument, reproducibility, and limitations essentially unchanged.
